newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 96 inflation nudged up by oil price - finmin.
newsitem.headline: French 96 inflation nudged up by oil price - finmin.

text.p: France's 1996 inflation figure of 1.7 percent announced by statistics office INSEE on Friday was above a 1.5 percent government forecast because of a big rise in oil prices late in the year, the finance ministry said.
Provisional data released by INSEE showed consumer prices rose 0.2 percent month-on-month in December and 1.7 percent year-on-year.
"This year-on-year result is very close to the one projected in the economic and financial report tied to the (1997) budget law," said the ministry statement.
"The slight difference is mainly due to the strong late-year rise in oil prices and the rate per barrel on international markets," it added.

The ministry said movements in oil prices and the dollar resulted in a 6.6 percent rise in energy prices in 1996, but said this was partly offset by smaller price rises for public and private services and for tobacco compared with 1994.
The ministry said 1995 was an exceptional year because of the effect of the increase in the rate of value added tax in that year.
